titulo: I will have finished, I would have gone
intro: Two compound tenses: the future perfect and the conditional perfect.
p.habré.consejo: With a participle it says that something will be finished: «habré terminado». The h is silent.
p.habrá.consejo: With a participle it can be a finished future or a guess: «habrá salido» means «he surely went out».
p.habría.consejo: With a participle it says what would have happened, but did not: «habría ido». It sounds a-BRI-a.
p.habrías.consejo: It is «habría» for tú: «tú habrías venido». The accent on «í» separates the vowels: a-BRI-as.
p.para entonces.consejo: It marks the limit in the future: «para entonces habré terminado» means «before that moment».
p.para el viernes.consejo: Here «para» sets a deadline: «para el viernes lo habré terminado».
p.en su lugar.consejo: Change «su» according to the person: «en mi lugar», «en tu lugar», «en su lugar».
p.avisar.consejo: A regular -ar verb. The v sounds like b: a-bi-SAR.
p.proyecto.consejo: It is masculine: «el proyecto». It is written with y and sounds pro-YEK-to.
p.habrá pasado.consejo: It is a guess about something recent: «¿qué habrá pasado?» asks what may have happened.
p.perder el tren.consejo: «Perder» is used for a train, a plane or an opportunity. Its opposite is «coger el tren».
b1.texto:
The **future perfect** is **habré, habrás, habrá, habremos, habréis, habrán** + participle. It says that something will be finished before a future moment:

- **Para el viernes habré terminado.**

It also serves to guess about the recent past:

- Marta has not come. **Habrá perdido** the train.

The **conditional perfect** is **habría, habrías, habría, habríamos, habríais, habrían** + participle. It says what would have happened, but did not:

- Yo **habría ido**, pero no pude.
b2.f0.texto: When do you finish the project?
b2.f1.texto: I will have finished it by Friday.
b2.f4.texto: She must have missed the train.
b2.f5.texto: In her place, I would have let someone know.
b2.f7.texto: She surely has had a good reason.
b4.titulo: Three uses of the compound tenses
b4.texto:
These tenses are formed with **haber** (in the future or conditional) and a **participle**. They have three uses:

1. **An action finished before a future moment**: Para entonces habremos terminado.
2. **A guess about the recent past**: Habrá salido muy temprano. (He probably left.)
3. **What would have happened and did not**: En tu lugar, yo no habría dicho nada.

The conditional perfect also serves for a reproach: **Me lo habrías podido decir**.

The auxiliary always stays next to the participle, and the participle does not change: habré hecho, habrías dicho, habrá puesto.
b4.e0.texto: By then we will have finished.
b4.e1.texto: He must have left home very early.
b4.e2.texto: In your place, I would not have said anything.
b5.f0.texto: On the deserted platform, a cold wind drags dry leaves and scraps of paper.
b5.f1.texto: The big station clock hangs motionless over the empty tracks.
b5.f2.texto: Far away, in the fog, two red lights shine.
b5.f3.texto: Marta runs along the platform with the suitcase in her hand.
b5.f4.texto: Her breath turns into mist in the icy air.
b5.f5.texto: The doors of the last carriage close with a metallic sigh.
b5.f6.texto: With five more minutes, she would have arrived on time.
b5.f7.texto: She stays still beside the suitcase and watches the red lights.
b5.f8.texto: Now the phone buzzes in her pocket with a message from Pablo.
b5.f9.texto: Marta smiles, tired, and puts the phone away without answering.
b6.o0.refuerzo: «Terminaré» places the end on Friday, not before.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes! The future perfect marks something finished before that day.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Terminé» is past; you speak of a Friday that has not come yet.
b6.pregunta: Which sentence says it will be finished before Friday?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: «habré» is the future of «haber» for yo.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Habría» is conditional and speaks of something that did not happen.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Hube» is a very old past and is hardly used.
b7.pregunta: It is something that will be done before Friday.
b8.frase: Yo en tu lugar habría avisado
b8.traduccion: In your place, I would have let someone know
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Saldrá» looks ahead: it is future, not past.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Había salido» states a fact; it is not a guess.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Exactly! «Habrá salido» guesses that he probably went out.
b9.pregunta: He does not answer. Which sentence guesses something that already happened?
b10.o0.refuerzo: «Habré» speaks of the future; here you imagine a different past.
b10.o1.refuerzo: That's it: the conditional perfect says what would have happened.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Había avisado» reports a fact; it imagines nothing.
b10.pregunta: You imagine what you would have done in her situation.
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I would have gone.»
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Habría ido» says exactly the opposite: he did not go.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Well done! The conditional perfect speaks of what did not happen.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «No pude» closes the possibility: he is no longer going.
b12.pregunta: «Habría ido, pero no pude.» Did he go?
p.terminas.consejo: Present of «terminar» for tú. The ending -as shows that tú is speaking to.
p.perdido.consejo: Participle of «perder». With «habrá» it makes a guess: «habrá perdido el tren».
p.avisado.consejo: Participle of «avisar». With «habría» it says what you would have done: «habría avisado».
p.motivo.consejo: It is masculine: «un motivo». The v and the b sound the same, so «motivo» uses a v.
p.habremos.consejo: Future of «haber» for nosotros. With a participle it says what will be finished: «habremos terminado».
p.desierto.consejo: It means empty of people. The «ie» sounds as one beat: de-SYER-to. It is also a noun: «desierto».
p.arrastra.consejo: From «arrastrar». The rr is strong: a-RRAS-tra. A wind can drag things along the ground.
p.secas.consejo: Feminine plural of «seco». It agrees with «hojas». The c sounds like k before a.
p.trozos.consejo: Plural of «trozo». The z sounds like th before o: TRO-thos. Same family as «romper».
p.inmóvil.consejo: The same for masculine and feminine. The accent marks the stress: in-MÓ-bil. The plural is «inmóviles».
p.vías.consejo: Plural of «vía». The accent separates the vowels: BÍ-as. The v sounds like b.
p.respiración.consejo: It is feminine: «la respiración». It ends in -ión, so the accent marks the end: rres-pi-ra-THYON.
p.helado.consejo: It comes from «hielo». The h is silent: e-LA-do. As a noun, «helado» is ice cream.
p.último.consejo: The accent shows the stress on the first syllable: ÚL-ti-mo. Before a masculine noun it stays «último».
p.vagón.consejo: It is masculine: «el vagón». The accent marks the end; in the plural it disappears: «vagones».
p.cierran.consejo: From «cerrar»: the e becomes «ie» in ellos. The rr is strong: THYE-rran.
p.suspiro.consejo: It is masculine: «un suspiro». The verb is «suspirar». The stress falls on «PI».
p.quieta.consejo: Feminine of «quieto». The qu sounds k and the u is silent: KYE-ta. «Quedarse quieta» is to stay still.
p.vibra.consejo: From «vibrar». The v sounds like b: BI-bra. A phone can «vibrar» when it receives a message.
